newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish govt lifts 1996/97 forecasts of GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: Swedish govt lifts 1996/97 forecasts of GDP growth.

text.p: The Swedish government said in its 1997 budget on Friday that it now saw gross domestic product (GDP) rising by 1.6 percent in 1996.
This compared with a forecast of 1.4 percent at its last budget in April this year.
The government also forecast GDP growth in 1997 at 2.3 percent compared to an April forecast of 2.0 percent.
"The Swedish economy grew more rapidly than expected during the first half of 1996," a Finance Ministry statement said.
"Demand from export markets increased markedly. A gradual improvement in economic activity in Europe is expected in the second half of 1996."
The department said GDP grwoth this year was anticipated to be mainly export and investment driven.
"The downturn in the stocks cycles will significantly limit growth."
The statement said a low inflation rate, lower interest rates and increased confidence in general government finances should stimulate private consumption next year.
The government predicted GDP growth would be 2.6 percent in 1998, 2.4 percent in 1999 and 2.0 percent in 2000.
